questions.knowledge_point: Differentiating Inverse Reciprocal Trigonometric Functions
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccsc$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sqrt{x}-2arccscx) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}-2(-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}+\frac{2}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccot$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(2x+arccotx) \\  & =2+(-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}) \\  & =2-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent to the curve at $x=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={y}^{′}(0) & =2-\frac{1}{1+{0}^{2}} \\  & =2-1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the curve $f(x)=-7arccscx$ at $x=\sqrt{5}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arccsc$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)=-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(-7arccscx) \\  & =-7\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =\frac{7}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=f(x)$ at $x=\sqrt{5}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(\sqrt{5}) & =\frac{7}{|\sqrt{5}|\sqrt{{\sqrt{5}}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5-1}} \\  & =\frac{7}{2\sqrt{5}}.\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arcsec$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec\,x)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5arcsec({x}^{2}+3)) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+3) \\  & =5\cdot \frac{1}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}\cdot (2x) \\  & =\frac{10x}{|{x}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({x}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of the tangent line to the curve at $x=2$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m={f}^{′}(2) & =\frac{10(2)}{|{2}^{2}+3|\sqrt{({2}^{2}+3)^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{20}{|7|\sqrt{49-1}} \\  & =\frac{20}{7\sqrt{48}} \\  & =\frac{20}{7\cdot 4\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{5}{7\sqrt{3}} \\  & =\frac{5\sqrt{3}}{21}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the slope of the tangent line to the function $y=arcsec({x}^{3}-6x)$ at $x=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of $arcsec$ is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx)=\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.
$$

Using the chain rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsec({x}^{3}-6x)) \\  & =\frac{1}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}-6x) \\  & =\frac{1}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\cdot (3{x}^{2}-6) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}-6}{|{x}^{3}-6x|\sqrt{({x}^{3}-6x)^{2}-1}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line to the curve at $x=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(1)\text{ } & =\frac{3(1)^{2}-6}{|{1}^{3}-6(1)|\sqrt{({1}^{3}-6(1))^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{-3}{|-5|\sqrt{(1-6)^{2}-1}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\sqrt{24}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\sqrt{4\cdot 6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\cdot \sqrt{4}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{5\cdot 2\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3}{10\sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{10\sqrt{6}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =-\frac{3\sqrt{6}}{60} \\  & =-\frac{\sqrt{6}}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule and the formula above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x}\cdot arccot\,x) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({e}^{x})\cdot arccot\,x+{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccot\,x) \\  & ={e}^{x}\,arccot\,x+{e}^{x}\cdot (-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}) \\  & ={e}^{x}\,arccot\,x-\frac{{e}^{x}}{1+{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}

The formulae for the derivatives of $arccsc$ and $arcsec$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx) & =-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}, \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) & =\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule and the formulae above, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =arcsecx\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arccscx)+arccscx\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(arcsecx) \\  & =arcsecx\cdot (-\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}})+arccscx\cdot (\frac{1}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}) \\  & =-\frac{arcsecx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}+\frac{arccscx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}} \\  & =\frac{arccscx-arcsecx}{|x|\sqrt{{x}^{2}-1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Here, we let $u(x)=arccotx$ and $v(x)=x$, and apply the quotient rule.

We use the formulae

$$
{u}^{′}(x)=-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{and}\,{v}^{′}(x)=1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{{u}^{′}(x)\cdot v(x)-u(x)\cdot {v}^{′}(x)}{[v(x)]^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\cdot x-arccotx\cdot 1}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-\frac{x}{1+{x}^{2}}-arccotx}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{(\frac{x+(1+{x}^{2})arccotx}{1+{x}^{2}})}{{x}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{x+(1+{x}^{2})arccotx}{{x}^{2}(1+{x}^{2})}.\end{aligned}
$$
